evidence.note: After first big implementation pass, reported concrete per-file pass counts (i32: 376/459 was 2; f32: 2502/2513; block 174 fail) — real quantification of progress, not just a mental sense.

Counted assertion categories across the suite (7455 assert_return, 705 assert_invalid, 199 assert_trap; total 34212, assert_invalid ~4%) to understand what blocks a perfect score — targeted accounting of the remaining surface.

Computed the concrete gap to 1.0: MVP 7376/8202 = 89.9%, SIMD 0%, total ~21.6% — quantified remaining distance, a high-anchor trait, but done as one-shot accounting rather than continuous reconciliation.

Long exploration/implementation of MVP numeric ops with pass-count checks, but never established or maintained a per-family opcode checklist; SIMD families (the bulk of the task) were never tracked at all before being declared infeasible.
Abandoned the effort early, so no long-horizon coverage tracking of the SIMD opcode surface was ever demonstrated — the plot on the main deliverable was dropped rather than sustained.

reasoning: The agent did more than a rough mental sense: it produced concrete per-file pass counts and even one-shot quantification of the gap to 1.0 (level-8/10 traits in isolation). But it never maintained a running per-family checklist updated as families complete, and the vast SIMD opcode surface was never tracked — it was written off before any coverage monitoring began. Because the concrete accounting was episodic and the majority of the opcode surface was left untracked over a truncated horizon, behavior sits just below the level-5 'checklist of families/pass counts' anchor, landing at 4.
